falsifiable_hypothesis: The current amplitude-target-global shrinker combines targetwise amplitude reliability, common reliability and global reliability to decide how much hierarchical structure to use, but it still applies the resulting contrast at the same nominal one-sided half-contrast scale in every outer partition. When either the global 24-vector or the common orientation mode is reliable, the final contrast estimate itself can be trusted more strongly. A parameter-free confidence amplification by 1+max(a_global,a_common) should reduce residual B-orientation bias without changing acquisition.
component_rule: Orientation A is leave-one-whole-patient bagged geometry. Orientation B starts from interpolated-jackknife geometry. No A/B prediction averaging occurs.
shrinkage_rule: Compute theta_amp, a_global and a_common exactly as in amplitude_target_global_hierarchical_js from the same three authenticated inner whole-patient bandwidth-0.7 OOF contrast vectors. Define confidence=max(a_global,a_common), amplification=1+confidence, theta_final=amplification*theta_amp, and q_B=q_B,interpolated_jackknife-0.5*theta_final. There is no scale menu, no per-target outer routing, no held-fold outcome use in the rule, and no protected data.

task_contract.ab_rule: average losses across separately costed A/B orientations; never average predictions
